description: What a scrub makes of a copy whose chunk does not hold what its hash says, or cannot be read on a disk that confirms, read again past the cache, its size and times unchanged: corrupt, repaired or moved to the trash; or its file a conflict, every version kept, nothing written. A copy never verified may never have held its file's content; a disk whose times do not tell two changes in one second apart gives an edit made in the second of the copy's last change the times its row has.

cases.note: verified, on a disk that holds a time to the nanosecond
verified, on NTFS, which holds a time to 100 ns
an ext4 made with 128-byte inodes holds whole seconds: an edit in place in the second of the copy's last change moves no time
a precision no check read vouches for nothing
never verified: nothing says it ever held its file's content
never verified, on a disk that holds whole seconds
